subject: HSS
title: World History and Geography: Ancient Civilizations
description: Students study the peoples and civilizations of the ancient world from early humans through the fall of Rome: Mesopotamia, Egypt and Kush, ancient Israel, Greece, India, China and Rome. They use maps, timelines, archaeology and primary sources (the Code of Hammurabi, Egyptian hymns, the Hebrew Bible, Pericles' Funeral Oration, Ashoka's edicts, the Analects, Roman law and more) to explain how geography, religion, government, trade and ideas shaped societies whose legacies remain today. Religions are studied academically, as the HSS Framework directs, to understand their history and influence.
framework: California History-Social Science Content Standards (Grade 6); 2016 CA History-Social Science Framework, Chapter 10

standards.6.1: Students describe what is known through archaeological studies of the early physical and cultural development of humankind from the Paleolithic era to the agricultural revolution.
standards.6.1.1: Describe the hunter-gatherer societies, including the development of tools and the use of fire.
standards.6.1.2: Identify the locations of human communities that populated the major regions of the world and describe how humans adapted to a variety of environments.
standards.6.1.3: Discuss the climatic changes and human modifications of the environment that gave rise to the domestication of plants and animals and new sources of clothing and shelter.
standards.6.2: Students analyze the geographic, political, economic, religious and social structures of the early civilizations of Mesopotamia, Egypt and Kush.
standards.6.2.1: Locate and describe the major river systems and the physical settings that supported permanent settlement and early civilizations.
standards.6.2.2: Trace the development of agricultural techniques that permitted economic surplus and the emergence of cities as centers of culture and power.
standards.6.2.3: Understand the relationship between religion and the social and political order in Mesopotamia and Egypt.
standards.6.2.4: Know the significance of Hammurabi's Code.
standards.6.2.5: Discuss the main features of Egyptian art and architecture.
standards.6.2.6: Describe the role of Egyptian trade in the eastern Mediterranean and Nile valley.
standards.6.2.7: Understand the significance of Queen Hatshepsut and Ramses the Great.
standards.6.2.8: Identify the location of the Kush civilization and describe its political, commercial and cultural relations with Egypt.
standards.6.2.9: Trace the evolution of language and its written forms.
standards.6.3: Students analyze the geographic, political, economic, religious and social structures of the Ancient Hebrews.
standards.6.3.1: Describe the origins and significance of Judaism as the first monotheistic religion based on the concept of one God who sets down moral laws for humanity.
standards.6.3.2: Identify the sources of the ethical teachings and central beliefs of Judaism and how they are reflected in the moral and ethical traditions of Western civilization.
standards.6.3.3: Explain the significance of Abraham, Moses, Naomi, Ruth, David and Yohanan ben Zaccai in the development of the Jewish religion.
standards.6.3.4: Discuss the locations of the settlements and movements of Hebrew peoples, including the Exodus, and outline the significance of the Exodus.
standards.6.3.5: Discuss how Judaism survived and developed despite continuing dispersion (the Diaspora), including the destruction of the Second Temple and the academy at Yavneh.
standards.6.4: Students analyze the geographic, political, economic, religious and social structures of the early civilizations of Ancient Greece.
standards.6.4.1: Discuss the connections between geography and the development of city-states in the region of the Aegean Sea, including patterns of trade and commerce.
standards.6.4.2: Trace the transition from tyranny and oligarchy to early democratic forms of government and back to dictatorship, including Pericles' Funeral Oration.
standards.6.4.3: State the key differences between Athenian, or direct, democracy and representative democracy.
standards.6.4.4: Explain the significance of Greek mythology to everyday life and literature, including Homer's Iliad and Odyssey and Aesop's Fables.
standards.6.4.5: Outline the founding, expansion and political organization of the Persian Empire.
standards.6.4.6: Compare and contrast life in Athens and Sparta, with emphasis on their roles in the Persian and Peloponnesian Wars.
standards.6.4.7: Trace the rise of Alexander the Great and the spread of Greek culture eastward and into Egypt.
standards.6.4.8: Describe the enduring contributions of important Greek figures in the arts and sciences (e.g., Hypatia, Socrates, Plato, Aristotle, Euclid, Thucydides).
standards.6.5: Students analyze the geographic, political, economic, religious and social structures of the early civilizations of India.
standards.6.5.1: Locate and describe the major river system and discuss the physical setting that supported the rise of this civilization.
standards.6.5.2: Discuss the significance of the Aryan (Indo-Aryan) migrations.
standards.6.5.3: Explain the major beliefs and practices of Brahmanism in India and how they evolved into early Hinduism.
standards.6.5.4: Outline the social structure of the caste system.
standards.6.5.5: Know the life and moral teachings of Buddha and how Buddhism spread in India, Ceylon and Central Asia.
standards.6.5.6: Describe the growth of the Maurya empire and the political and moral achievements of the emperor Asoka.
standards.6.5.7: Discuss important aesthetic and intellectual traditions (e.g., Sanskrit literature including the Bhagavad Gita; medicine; metallurgy; mathematics, including Hindu-Arabic numerals and zero).
standards.6.6: Students analyze the geographic, political, economic, religious and social structures of the early civilizations of China.
standards.6.6.1: Locate and describe the origins of Chinese civilization in the Huang-He Valley during the Shang Dynasty.
standards.6.6.2: Explain the geographic features of China that made governance and the spread of ideas and goods difficult and served to isolate the country.
standards.6.6.3: Know about the life of Confucius and the fundamental teachings of Confucianism and Daoism.
standards.6.6.4: Identify the political and cultural problems prevalent in the time of Confucius and how he sought to solve them.
standards.6.6.5: List the policies and achievements of the emperor Shi Huangdi in unifying northern China under the Qin Dynasty.
standards.6.6.6: Detail the political contributions of the Han Dynasty to the development of the imperial bureaucratic state and the expansion of the empire.
standards.6.6.7: Cite the significance of the trans-Eurasian 'silk roads' in the period of the Han Dynasty and Roman Empire and their locations.
standards.6.6.8: Describe the diffusion of Buddhism northward to China during the Han Dynasty.
standards.6.7: Students analyze the geographic, political, economic, religious and social structures during the development of Rome.
standards.6.7.1: Identify the location and describe the rise of the Roman Republic, including the importance of figures such as Aeneas, Romulus and Remus, Cincinnatus, Julius Caesar and Cicero.
standards.6.7.2: Describe the government of the Roman Republic and its significance (written constitution, tripartite government, checks and balances, civic duty).
standards.6.7.3: Identify the location of and reasons for the growth of Roman territories and how the empire fostered economic growth through currency and trade routes.
standards.6.7.4: Discuss the influence of Julius Caesar and Augustus in Rome's transition from republic to empire.
standards.6.7.5: Trace the migration of Jews around the Mediterranean region and the effects of their conflict with the Romans, including restrictions on their right to live in Jerusalem.
standards.6.7.6: Note the origins of Christianity in Jewish Messianic prophecies, the life and teachings of Jesus of Nazareth as described in the New Testament, and the contribution of Paul the Apostle.
standards.6.7.7: Describe the circumstances that led to the spread of Christianity in Europe and other Roman territories.
standards.6.7.8: Discuss the legacies of Roman art and architecture, technology and science, literature, language and law.
standards.CST.1: Analysis skill: Explain how major events are related to one another in time (chronological thinking, timelines, BCE/CE).
standards.CST.3: Analysis skill: Use a variety of maps and documents to identify physical and cultural features and explain historical migration and settlement patterns.
standards.REP.2: Analysis skill: Distinguish relevant from irrelevant information and essential from incidental information in historical narratives.
standards.REP.4: Analysis skill: Assess the credibility of primary and secondary sources and draw sound conclusions from them.
standards.HI.1: Analysis skill: Explain the central issues and problems from the past, placing people and events in a matrix of time and place.

units.title: Early Humankind and the Agricultural Revolution
units.big_idea: Archaeology reveals how early humans adapted to environments and how farming changed the way people lived.

units.title: Mesopotamia: The Fertile Crescent
units.big_idea: Rivers, surplus and writing allowed the first cities, kingdoms and written laws.

units.title: Ancient Egypt and Kush
units.big_idea: The Nile shaped a long-lasting civilization whose religion, rulers, art and trade linked it to Kush and the Mediterranean.

units.title: Ancient Israel and the Origins of Judaism
units.big_idea: The ancient Hebrews developed monotheism and ethical teachings that endured through exile and dispersion.

units.title: Ancient Greece
units.big_idea: Greek city-states experimented with government, fought for survival and produced ideas in art, science and philosophy still used today.

units.title: Ancient India
units.big_idea: From the Indus cities to the Maurya Empire, India developed major religions, a complex social structure and lasting achievements in mathematics and literature.

units.title: Ancient China
units.big_idea: China's geography, philosophies and dynasties created a unified bureaucratic state connected to the world by the Silk Roads.

units.title: Ancient Rome
units.big_idea: Rome grew from a republic to an empire whose law, language, engineering and religions shaped the Western world.

weeks.topic: Tools of the historian and geographer
objectives: Read maps with latitude and longitude
materials: long strip of paper for timeline

days.title: What is history?
days.work: Examine three family artifacts (photo, letter, object) and write what each reveals and what it cannot tell you.

days.title: Primary vs. secondary
days.work: Sort 12 sources (a diary, an encyclopedia article, a coin, a textbook) as primary or secondary and justify each.

days.title: Timelines and BCE/CE
days.work: Build a classroom-length timeline from 10,000 BCE to 500 CE that you will add to all year; practice calculating years between BCE and CE dates.

days.title: Map skills
days.work: Locate the seven continents, major rivers (Nile, Tigris, Euphrates, Indus, Huang He) and practice latitude/longitude coordinates.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on sources, timelines and map skills.

objectives: Explain the importance of tools and fire
materials: photos of stone tools (Smithsonian Human Origins)

days.title: Life on the move
days.work: Read about hunter-gatherer daily life and create a chart of food, shelter, tools and social roles.

days.title: Tool technology
days.work: Analyze images of Oldowan and Acheulean hand axes and explain how tools improved over time.

days.title: Fire
days.work: Write a paragraph explaining at least four ways controlling fire changed early human life.

days.title: Cave art
days.work: Study images of the Lascaux and Chauvet cave paintings and infer what they show about beliefs and daily life.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a 'day in the life' diary entry of a hunter-gatherer using at least six accurate details.

objectives: Trace human migration out of Africa

days.title: Out of Africa
days.work: Map the major human migration routes out of Africa with approximate dates.

days.title: Ice Age land bridges
days.work: Explain how lower sea levels during the Ice Age created Beringia and allowed people to reach the Americas.

days.title: Adapting to environments
days.work: Compare how people adapted clothing, shelter and food in the Arctic, desert and rainforest.

days.title: First Californians
days.work: Read about early evidence of people in California (e.g., Channel Islands sites) and add it to the timeline.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Map quiz on migration routes and a short answer on human adaptation.

objectives: Explain how climate change and domestication led to farming
Analyze effects of farming on society

days.title: Domestication
days.work: Read about the domestication of wheat, rice, maize and animals and map where each began.

days.title: Plant an experiment
days.work: Plant bean seeds and begin a growth log, reflecting on why early farmers chose to settle near their crops.

days.title: Catalhoyuk
days.work: Study an artist's reconstruction of Catalhoyuk and list evidence of permanent settlement and specialization.

days.title: Costs and benefits
days.work: Create a T-chart of the benefits and costs of farming vs. hunting and gathering.

days.title: Unit 1 test
days.work: Take the Unit 1 assessment and write a paragraph on how farming changed human life.

days.title: Land between rivers
days.work: Label a map of the Fertile Crescent with rivers, deserts, mountains and modern countries.

days.title: Irrigation model
days.work: Build an irrigation model in a tray of soil with a canal and test how water reaches 'fields'.

days.title: Floods and silt
days.work: Read about unpredictable Tigris-Euphrates floods and how Sumerians managed them with levees and canals.

days.title: Surplus and cities
days.work: Draw a cause-and-effect chain from irrigation to surplus to specialization to cities.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on Mesopotamian geography and agriculture.

objectives: Explain the link between religion and political order
materials: images of the Ziggurat of Ur and Standard of Ur

days.title: City-states
days.work: Read about Ur and Uruk and describe how a Sumerian city-state was organized.

days.title: Ziggurats
days.work: Build a model ziggurat from blocks or sugar cubes and explain its religious and political role.

days.title: Standard of Ur
days.work: Analyze the 'War' and 'Peace' sides of the Standard of Ur and infer the social hierarchy.

days.title: Social pyramid
days.work: Create a social pyramid of Sumerian society and explain how religion supported the rulers' power.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph using evidence from the Standard of Ur about Sumerian society.

weeks.topic: Writing and the Epic of Gilgamesh
materials: excerpts of the Epic of Gilgamesh (Fordham Sourcebook)

days.title: From tokens to writing
days.work: Read how clay tokens and pictographs evolved into cuneiform and make a three-stage chart.

days.title: Write cuneiform
days.work: Press your name and a short message in cuneiform wedges into a clay tablet using a stick.

days.title: Scribe school
days.work: Read about scribal schools and write a letter from a student scribe describing a day.

days.title: Gilgamesh
days.work: Read the flood episode of the Epic of Gilgamesh and discuss what it reveals about Mesopotamian beliefs.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on writing and short response on why writing mattered for government and trade.

objectives: Analyze Hammurabi's Code as a primary source

days.title: First empires
days.work: Read about Sargon of Akkad and Hammurabi of Babylon and map their empires.

days.title: Reading the Code
days.work: Read 20 laws from Hammurabi's Code and sort them into categories (property, family, trade, injury).

days.title: Fair or not?
days.work: Analyze how punishments differed by social class and debate whether the code was 'just' by Babylonian and by modern standards.

days.title: Stele analysis
days.work: Examine the stele image and explain why carving laws in public mattered.

days.title: Unit 2 test
days.work: Take the Unit 2 test with a document-based short essay on Hammurabi's Code.

objectives: Describe the Nile's geography and flooding
Explain how the Nile supported agriculture and unity
materials: Herodotus 'Egypt is the gift of the Nile' quote

days.title: Mapping the Nile
days.work: Label the Nile, delta, cataracts, Upper and Lower Egypt, and surrounding deserts on a map.

days.title: Hymn to the Nile
days.work: Read the 'Hymn to the Nile' and list what Egyptians thanked the river for.

days.title: Farming calendar
days.work: Make a circular calendar of the flood, planting and harvest seasons and explain the shaduf.

days.title: Unification
days.work: Read about Narmer (Menes) and the double crown and explain how the Nile helped unify Egypt.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Compare the Nile with the Tigris-Euphrates in a Venn diagram; quiz on Egyptian geography.

objectives: Explain the pharaoh's religious and political roles
materials: images of Giza and tomb paintings

days.title: God-king
days.work: Read about the pharaoh as a divine ruler and draw Egypt's social pyramid.

days.title: Mummify an apple
days.work: Begin an apple mummification experiment with salt and baking soda, weighing the slices first.

days.title: Book of the Dead
days.work: Read the 'Weighing of the Heart' scene and explain what it shows about Egyptian ethics.

days.title: Pyramids
days.work: Research how the Great Pyramid was built and who built it, then write a short explanation using two sources.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Weigh the apple slices, explain the results, and take a quiz on Egyptian religion and government.

materials: images of Abu Simbel and Deir el-Bahri

days.title: Hieroglyphs and the Rosetta Stone
days.work: Learn how the Rosetta Stone was deciphered and write your name in hieroglyphs in a cartouche.

days.title: Egyptian art rules
days.work: Analyze tomb paintings for composite view, hierarchical scale and symbolism, then draw a figure in Egyptian style.

days.title: Hatshepsut
days.work: Read about Hatshepsut's reign, trade expedition to Punt and temple, and why her images were later erased.

days.title: Ramses the Great
days.work: Examine Abu Simbel and the Battle of Kadesh accounts and decide what is history and what is propaganda.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph comparing the legacies of Hatshepsut and Ramses II.

weeks.topic: Trade and the Kingdom of Kush

days.title: Trade routes
days.work: Map Egyptian trade with Punt, Nubia, the Levant and Crete, listing goods exchanged.

days.title: Kush rises
days.work: Read about Kush and its resources (gold, ivory, ebony) and its conquest of Egypt under Piye.

days.title: Meroe
days.work: Compare the pyramids of Meroe with Giza and explain Meroe's ironworking industry.

days.title: Kush and Egypt
days.work: Create a timeline showing changing relations between Egypt and Kush (trade, conquest, cultural borrowing).

days.title: Unit 3 test
days.work: Take the Unit 3 test on Egypt and Kush.

objectives: Explain the roles of Abraham and Moses as described in the Hebrew Bible
materials: map of ancient Canaan and Egypt
Hebrew Bible excerpts: Genesis 12 and Exodus 20

days.title: Geography of Canaan
days.work: Map Abraham's journey from Ur to Canaan as described in Genesis and the location of ancient Israel.

days.title: Monotheism
days.work: Compare monotheism and polytheism and explain why historians consider Judaism's belief in one God significant.

days.title: The Exodus
days.work: Read the Exodus account and map the route; explain the significance of the Exodus in Jewish tradition and Passover.

days.title: The Ten Commandments
days.work: Read Exodus 20 and categorize the commandments as duties to God and to other people; connect to later legal traditions.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on early Hebrew history and beliefs.

objectives: Describe the kingdom of David and Solomon
Identify sources of Jewish ethical teachings

days.title: Naomi and Ruth
days.work: Read the Book of Ruth and explain what it teaches about loyalty and kindness to strangers.

days.title: David and Solomon
days.work: Read about King David and Solomon's Temple and add the united monarchy to the timeline.

days.title: Prophets and justice
days.work: Read Micah 6:8 and Amos 5:24 and explain the prophets' teachings on justice and righteousness.

days.title: Western traditions
days.work: Find connections between Jewish ethical teachings (Sabbath, care for the poor, rule of law) and later Western traditions.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph explaining one key Jewish ethical teaching and its influence, citing a source.

objectives: Trace the movements of the Jewish people
materials: map of the Mediterranean and Near East
image of the Arch of Titus

days.title: Babylonian exile
days.work: Read about the destruction of the First Temple and exile to Babylon and map the movement.

days.title: Return and Second Temple
days.work: Read about Cyrus of Persia permitting return and the rebuilding of the Temple.

days.title: Roman destruction
days.work: Analyze the Arch of Titus relief showing the Temple's treasures being carried away in 70 CE.

days.title: Yavneh and survival
days.work: Read about Yohanan ben Zaccai's academy at Yavneh and explain how study, synagogues and rabbis preserved Judaism.

days.title: Unit 4 test
days.work: Take the Unit 4 test with a map of the Diaspora.

objectives: Explain how geography encouraged independent city-states

days.title: Mountains and seas
days.work: Make a salt-dough relief map of Greece showing mountains and coastlines.

days.title: The polis
days.work: Explain how mountains led to independent city-states and diagram a polis with acropolis and agora.

days.title: Minoans and Mycenaeans
days.work: Read about Knossos and Mycenae and compare the two earlier Aegean cultures.

days.title: Trade and colonies
days.work: Map Greek colonies around the Mediterranean and Black Sea and list traded goods (olive oil, wine, pottery).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a CER-style paragraph: How did geography shape Greek life?

days.title: Forms of government
days.work: Create a chart defining monarchy, aristocracy, oligarchy, tyranny and democracy with Greek examples.

days.title: Athenian democracy
days.work: Read about Solon and Cleisthenes and explain who could and could not participate as citizens.

days.title: Ostracism
days.work: Hold a mock ostracism vote with family using paper 'ostraka' and discuss its purpose.

days.title: Pericles' Funeral Oration
days.work: Read an excerpt and identify three values Pericles praised about Athenian democracy.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a comparison of Athenian direct democracy and U.S. representative democracy; quiz on government forms.

weeks.topic: Athens, Sparta and the Persian Wars
materials: Herodotus excerpts on Marathon and Thermopylae

days.title: Sparta vs. Athens
days.work: Read about education, women's roles and government in Sparta and Athens and complete a comparison chart.

days.title: Persian Empire
days.work: Map the Persian Empire under Cyrus and Darius and describe satrapies, the Royal Road and tolerance policies.

days.title: Marathon and Thermopylae
days.work: Read Herodotus's accounts and evaluate him as a source (what bias might he have?).

days.title: Salamis
days.work: Explain how Athenian naval power won at Salamis and diagram the battle.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Semester 1 cumulative review quiz covering early humans through the Persian Wars.

weeks.topic: Golden Age and the Peloponnesian War
objectives: Explain causes and effects of the Peloponnesian War

days.title: Golden Age
days.work: Read about Pericles' Athens and the building of the Parthenon and list achievements.

days.title: Delian League
days.work: Explain how the Delian League turned into an Athenian empire and why Sparta felt threatened.

days.title: War and plague
days.work: Read Thucydides' description of the plague of Athens and explain its effect on the war.

days.title: Consequences
days.work: Create a cause-and-effect chart of the Peloponnesian War and its result: a weakened Greece.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on the Golden Age and Peloponnesian War.

weeks.topic: Greek myths, literature and the arts
objectives: Explain the role of mythology in Greek life
Identify Greek words and symbols in modern life
materials: photos of Doric, Ionic and Corinthian columns

days.title: Gods and daily life
days.work: Read about the Olympian gods, festivals and the Olympic Games and explain how religion shaped Greek life.

days.title: Aesop's Fables
days.work: Read five of Aesop's Fables and write the moral of each, then write your own fable.

days.title: Greek theater
days.work: Learn the parts of a Greek theater, tragedy vs. comedy, and make a Greek drama mask.

days.title: Columns hunt
days.work: Identify Doric, Ionic and Corinthian columns and find examples on buildings in your community (courthouses, banks).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: List 10 modern words, brands or symbols from Greek mythology and explain their origins.

objectives: Trace Alexander's empire and Hellenistic culture

days.title: Socrates, Plato, Aristotle
days.work: Read about the three philosophers and practice the Socratic method by questioning a family member about 'What is fairness?'.

days.title: Scientists
days.work: Research Euclid, Archimedes, Hippocrates and Hypatia and make trading cards for each.

days.title: Alexander the Great
days.work: Map Alexander's conquests and explain how he spread Greek culture into Egypt and Asia.

days.title: Alexandria
days.work: Read about the Library and Lighthouse of Alexandria and do one of Euclid's compass-and-straightedge constructions.

days.title: Unit 5 test
days.work: Take the Unit 5 test on Ancient Greece.

objectives: Describe the geography of the Indian subcontinent
materials: images of Mohenjo-daro and Indus seals

days.title: Geography and monsoons
days.work: Map the Indus and Ganges rivers, Himalayas and Deccan Plateau and explain the monsoon cycle.

days.title: Planned cities
days.work: Study a plan of Mohenjo-daro and list evidence of planning (grid streets, drains, Great Bath).

days.title: Mystery of the seals
days.work: Examine Indus seals and explain why the script is still undeciphered.

days.title: Decline theories

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on Indian geography and the Indus civilization.

weeks.topic: Indo-Aryan migrations, Brahmanism and early Hinduism
objectives: Explain the significance of Indo-Aryan migrations
Describe beliefs of early Hinduism and the varna/caste system
materials: Rig Veda Hymn of Creation excerpt

days.title: Indo-Aryan migrations
days.work: Read about the Indo-Aryan migrations and the Vedas and explain their effect on language and religion.

days.title: Brahmanism
days.work: Read the Rig Veda 'Hymn of Creation' and discuss the role of Brahmin priests and rituals.

days.title: Hindu beliefs
days.work: Create a graphic organizer explaining Brahman, karma, dharma, reincarnation and moksha.

days.title: Social structure
days.work: Diagram the four varnas and jati system, and discuss how the system shaped daily life and limited mobility.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a paragraph explaining how Brahmanism evolved into Hinduism with two pieces of evidence.

weeks.topic: The Buddha and the spread of Buddhism

days.work: Read the story of Siddhartha Gautama and create a storyboard of key events leading to enlightenment.

days.title: Teachings
days.work: Explain the Four Noble Truths and Eightfold Path in your own words.

days.title: Dhammapada

days.title: Spread of Buddhism
days.work: Map the spread of Buddhism to Sri Lanka (Ceylon), Central Asia and beyond.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Compare Hinduism and Buddhism in a Venn diagram; quiz on Buddhism.

weeks.topic: The Maurya Empire and Indian achievements
objectives: Describe Ashoka's political and moral achievements
materials: images of the Lion Capital of Ashoka

days.title: Maurya Empire
days.work: Map the Maurya Empire under Chandragupta and describe how it was governed.

days.title: Ashoka's edicts
days.work: Read three Rock Edicts of Ashoka and identify the values he promoted after the Kalinga war.

days.title: Lion Capital

days.title: Indian achievements
days.work: Research Indian contributions (zero and Hindu-Arabic numerals, metallurgy, medicine, the Bhagavad Gita) and make an illustrated chart.

days.work: Take the Unit 6 test on ancient India.

days.title: Shang bronzes
days.work: Analyze Shang bronze vessels and explain what they reveal about technology and ancestor worship.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on Chinese geography and the Shang.

weeks.topic: Zhou, Mandate of Heaven, Confucius and Laozi
objectives: Describe Confucianism and Daoism and the problems they addressed

days.title: Mandate of Heaven
days.work: Draw the dynastic cycle and explain how the Zhou used the Mandate of Heaven to justify rule.

days.title: Warring States
days.work: Read about disorder in the Warring States period and list problems Confucius saw in society.

days.title: The Analects
days.work: Read 10 sayings from the Analects and explain the five relationships and filial piety.

days.title: Daoism
days.work: Read passages of the Dao De Jing and compare Daoist ideas about nature and government with Confucian ideas.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a dialogue between Confucius and Laozi about how to fix a troubled kingdom.

weeks.topic: The Qin Dynasty and Shi Huangdi
objectives: List Shi Huangdi's policies and achievements

days.title: Unifying China
days.work: Read about Qin Shi Huangdi's unification and list his standardization policies (writing, coins, weights, axles).

days.title: Legalism
days.work: Compare Legalist ideas with Confucianism and discuss the burning of books.

days.title: Great Wall
days.work: Map the early walls and explain the costs to the workers who built them.

days.title: Terracotta army
days.work: Study the terracotta army and sculpt a small clay soldier showing individual features.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write an evaluation: was Shi Huangdi a great leader or a tyrant? Use evidence for both sides.

weeks.topic: The Han Dynasty and the Silk Roads
objectives: Explain the significance of the Silk Roads and spread of Buddhism to China

days.title: Han government
days.work: Read about the Han civil service exams and explain how Confucian ideas shaped the bureaucracy.

days.title: Han inventions
days.work: Make recycled paper with scrap paper, a blender and a screen, and list other Han inventions (seismograph, wheelbarrow).

days.title: Silk Roads
days.work: Map the Silk Roads from Chang'an to Rome and list goods and ideas exchanged in each direction.

days.title: Buddhism comes to China
days.work: Trace how Buddhism traveled to China along the Silk Roads and how it blended with Chinese traditions.

days.title: Unit 7 test
days.work: Take the Unit 7 test on ancient China.

weeks.assessment: Silk Roads map and Unit 7 test.

objectives: Distinguish legend from history in Rome's founding
materials: Livy's account of Romulus and Remus (excerpt)

days.title: Italy's geography
days.work: Map the Italian peninsula, Tiber River, seven hills and Mediterranean location, and explain advantages for Rome.

days.title: Legends
days.work: Read Livy's account of Romulus and Remus and the Aeneas legend; separate legend from archaeological evidence.

days.title: Etruscans and Greeks
days.work: Identify what Rome borrowed from Etruscans and Greeks (arches, alphabet, gods).

days.title: Cincinnatus
days.work: Read the story of Cincinnatus and explain the Roman value of civic duty; connect to George Washington.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on early Rome and legend vs. history.

objectives: Describe the structure of the Republic's government
Compare it to the U.S. government

days.title: Patricians and plebeians
days.work: Read about the Conflict of the Orders and explain how plebeians gained rights.

days.title: Three branches
days.work: Diagram consuls, Senate and assemblies and show checks and balances among them.

days.title: Twelve Tables
days.work: Read selected laws of the Twelve Tables and explain why written law mattered (compare with Hammurabi).

days.title: Rome and the U.S.
days.work: Compare the Roman Republic with the U.S. government in a chart (veto, Senate, written law).

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write an essay paragraph on the Roman Republic's influence on American government; quiz on vocabulary.

objectives: Explain the expansion of Roman territory
Analyze the roles of Julius Caesar and Augustus

days.title: Punic Wars
days.work: Map the Punic Wars and Hannibal's route and explain how victory made Rome a Mediterranean power.

days.title: Crisis in the Republic
days.work: Read about the gap between rich and poor, the Gracchi and Cicero's defense of the Republic.

days.title: Julius Caesar
days.work: Read Plutarch's account of Caesar crossing the Rubicon and his assassination; debate whether he was a hero or threat.

days.title: Augustus
days.work: Read excerpts of the Res Gestae and identify how Augustus presented his power while keeping republican forms.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Create a timeline from 509 BCE to 27 CE and take a quiz on the republic's fall.

weeks.topic: Life and economy in the Roman Empire
objectives: Describe how the empire fostered trade
materials: map of Roman roads and trade

days.title: Roads and trade
days.work: Map Roman roads and sea trade routes and list goods from each province.

days.title: Roman coins
days.work: Analyze images of Roman coins and explain how a common currency helped the economy and spread imperial messages.

days.title: Daily life
days.work: Read about family life, slavery, schools and entertainment and compare a rich and a poor Roman's day.

days.title: Build an aqueduct
days.work: Build a cardboard aqueduct with a gentle slope that carries water 1 meter, measuring the drop.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Quiz on the Roman economy and daily life.

weeks.topic: Judea under Rome and the origins of Christianity
objectives: Trace Jewish migration and conflict with Rome
Describe the origins and spread of Christianity

days.title: Judea and Rome
days.work: Read about Roman rule in Judea, the Jewish revolts, and Rome's ban on Jews living in Jerusalem; map Jewish communities around the Mediterranean.

days.title: Jesus of Nazareth
days.work: Read the Sermon on the Mount and summarize key teachings of Jesus as described in the New Testament.

days.title: Paul's journeys
days.work: Map Paul's missionary journeys and explain his role in spreading Christian beliefs to non-Jews.

days.title: From persecution to official religion
days.work: Create a timeline from early persecution to Constantine's Edict of Milan and Theodosius, and explain why Christianity spread.

days.title: Review & check
days.work: Write a short explanation of three factors that helped Christianity spread through the Roman Empire.

weeks.topic: Roman legacy and the decline of the West
objectives: Explain causes of the Western Empire's decline
materials: images of the Pantheon and Colosseum

days.title: Architecture and engineering
days.work: Compare the Pantheon and Colosseum with modern buildings and identify Roman arches, domes and concrete.

days.title: Latin everywhere
days.work: Find 20 English words with Latin roots and translate common Latin mottos (e.g., California's 'Eureka' is Greek; the U.S. 'E pluribus unum' is Latin).

days.title: Roman law
days.work: Identify Roman legal principles still used today (innocent until proven guilty, rights of citizens).

days.title: Decline and fall
days.work: Read about the division of the empire and the fall of the West in 476 CE and rank causes by importance.

days.title: Unit review
days.work: Take the Unit 8 test on Ancient Rome.

weeks.topic: Legacies of the ancient world: final project

days.title: Choose a legacy
days.work: Choose one ancient legacy (writing, law, democracy, mathematics, religion, engineering) to trace across at least three civilizations.

days.title: Research
days.work: Gather evidence including at least two primary sources from the year and take notes.

days.title: Create
days.work: Create a museum exhibit poster or slide show connecting the legacy to life in California today.

days.title: Present
days.work: Present your exhibit to family or co-op as a museum docent and answer questions.

days.title: Final assessment
days.work: Complete the year-end timeline and take a cumulative final assessment on all seven civilizations.

weeks.assessment: Legacy project rubric and cumulative final.
